### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **5** documentable anchor(s).

**7** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/wire-format.mdx`  _(via /meta/object/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via /meta/object/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/formulas.mdx`  _(via /meta/object/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/deployment/production-readiness.mdx`  _(via /meta/object/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/http-protocol.mdx`  _(via /meta/object/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/state-machine.mdx`  _(via /meta/object/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/ui/forms.mdx`  _(via /meta/object/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via /meta/object/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via /meta/object/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via /meta/object/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **171** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 59547058aeb3eccde6f267293367dabf5ef82e59` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7c1a3044673f58300ebeed81119a2aa297eacc45` — the merge of head `cd36d2103e04e824c8dbb0dc973e87a0709dc2bf` into base `59547058aeb3eccde6f267293367dabf5ef82e59`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7c1a3044673f58300ebeed81119a2aa297eacc45 && git checkout 7c1a3044673f58300ebeed81119a2aa297eacc45
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 59547058aeb3eccde6f267293367dabf5ef82e59 cd36d2103e04e824c8dbb0dc973e87a0709dc2bf && git checkout -B drift-repro 59547058aeb3eccde6f267293367dabf5ef82e59 && git merge --no-ff cd36d2103e04e824c8dbb0dc973e87a0709dc2bf

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 59547058aeb3eccde6f267293367dabf5ef82e59
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 59547058aeb3eccde6f267293367dabf5ef82e59` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b45e4528df7096902b522423304ffaa5bec9e5f5`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts + packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-routes.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-action-activation-reads.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/object-schema-fls.ts, content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx

Rendered 2026-10-30T12:46Z on the schema face (`reviewFace` hits: `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`). Inputs: card #28044 (body + 3 comments), PR #28094 body, file list and net diff against `main` `8cb8c7f4`, the check-runs on the head. The remainder of the diff (`.changeset/*`, the `.test.ts`, the generated `protocol.mdx`) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at TIER_DEFAULT; the rest code was READ to judge the schema file, not reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set**: unchanged — right. No request shape, header or query moves; `GetMetaItemResponseSchema` and `GetMetaItemCachedResponseSchema` keep every key and type (only one `.describe()` string changes).
- **Public surface, HTTP behaviour**: a cached `GET /meta/object/:name` that carries `disabledActions` is now answerable `304` — right. Read in `meta-item-read-routes.ts` on the head: `besideJudged` is now `Object.keys(cachedRegistration).length > 0` (flow `registration` alone stands the 304 down), and the `If-None-Match` compare at the fingerprinted ETag runs for objects (`audienceFolds`). The protocol's own `ifNoneMatch` is already `undefined` for objects, so `getMetaItemCached` never judges them; the REST compare is the one judge.
- **Validator**: the served list is folded as a fifth dimension — right. `cachedDisabledActionsFingerprint(cachedDisabledActions.disabledActions)` hashes exactly the value placed in `cachedBeside`, so the ETag describes the representation sent (the #16525 lesson the card names). `undefined` folds `''` and `foldVisibilityFingerprintIntoEtag(etag, '')` returns `etag` unchanged, so a no-ledger object keeps its byte-identical ETag; `[]` goes through `objectFieldVisibilityFingerprint(['[]'])`, a one-element input, so it hashes to a non-empty dimension and absent ≠ `[]`. Order is deterministic: `switchedOffActionsOf` (`protocol-action-activation-reads.ts`) walks `body.actions` in declaration order, so the same switch set always serialises the same way and a 304 is not lost to ordering.
- **Response body**: unchanged — right; `cachedEnvelope` and `translateMetaEnvelope` inputs are untouched.
- **`GET /meta/object` (list read)**: the dev's claim that it has no cached/ETag door holds — `meta-collection-routes.ts` on the head contains no ETag, `If-None-Match` or 304 handling, so nothing there to fold or pin.
- **Generated docs**: `content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx:1462` follows the new describe string exactly; no other generated line moved — right.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/28044-object-read-etag-folds-disabled-actions.md`: `@objectstack/rest: patch`, `@objectstack/spec: patch` — matches what the diff publishes (a behaviour fix in `rest`; a describe-string change in `spec` that ships in the generated docs and `.d.ts`). ⛔ Not `skip-changeset`, correctly: both are released packages.
- `Clause-②: no` on the PR body and in the changeset body, no arm — the closed spelling `clause2-line.mjs` reads; correct, since the accept set and the response shape do not widen or narrow (a 304 the route already answered for other objects is not a surface change).
- `Metadata-protocol: none` on both carriers — correct: nothing an author can write changes. AGENTS.md step 3: kind `none` ⇒ `patch`. ✓ Both lines present on both carriers; the `Check Changeset` and `PR-body guards` check-runs are green.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flag: `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` left to CI → answered by the head's check-runs below (`Lint · CI, release & engine gates` green; `Build Core` still pending at render time).
- Dev flag: the list read has no cached door → verified in the tree (①), answered.
- Card: "a possible touch in `packages/metadata-protocol`" → not needed; the protocol's `disabledActions === undefined` stand-down at `protocol.ts:14562` is unreachable from the REST object door (REST passes `ifNoneMatch: undefined` under `audienceFolds`) and remains correct for any other caller of `getMetaItemCached`. Answered.
- Card: "Correct the two docblocks' 'never answered 304' sentence in the same PR" → NOT met on this head; see ④ (must-fix). The seat's claim narrowed its spec surface to the one `.describe()` string, but the card's requirement and the file's own consistency are the standard here.
- Card `open_questions`: none filed. No other dev flag.
- Check-runs on `b45e4528` at render: green — Auto Label, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint & Repo Gates, Lint · CI/release/engine, Lint · ESLint, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling, Lint · scoped ×3, Live E2E UI, PR-body guards, Plan Test Core shards, Spec property liveness, Test UI, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · source gates. **Still pending**: Build Core, Build & E2E UI, Test Core 1/8–8/8, Type Check UI, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · workspace. No failure.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`, judged against the card's ruling and its first consumer, `packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-routes.ts` on this head.

- The changed `.describe()` on `GetMetaItemResponseSchema.disabledActions` ("read live and folded into the ETag, so a cached read revalidates to 304 only while the switched-off set is unchanged; it is absent on a draft read") now tells the truth about the REST door: the list IS folded (`disabledActionsFingerprint` is the outermost `foldVisibilityFingerprintIntoEtag` argument at the ETag build), a 304 comes back only when `normalizeIfNoneMatch(If-None-Match)` equals the folded value, and that value moves whenever the served list moves (off, on, attach, detach). The rest of the sentence (presence only on an `object` read with a ledger, `[]` vs absent, draft read absent, beside `item`) is unchanged and still true. ✓
- **MUST-FIX (FAIL)** — left-behind contradiction in the same hits file. The docblock above `GetMetaItemResponseSchema` (head lines 636–639) still reads: "**On the cached default door too, out of the ETag.** A read that carries it is never answered 304, for the reason {@link GetMetaItemCachedResponseSchema} gives for `registration`." On this head that is false for the door it names (the cached default door answers 304 and the list is in its ETag), and it sits 100 lines above a `.describe()` that says the opposite. This is exactly the sentence card #28044 required corrected in the same PR ("Correct the two docblocks' 'never answered 304' sentence"), and it ships as TSDoc on the exported schema. Fix: rewrite the bullet to "On the cached default door too, folded into its ETag: a 304 comes back only while the switched-off set is unchanged (the REST door folds the served list; `GetMetaItemCachedResponseSchema`'s own `etag` does not carry it)".
- **SHOULD-FIX** — `GetMetaItemCachedResponseSchema` (head lines 2379–2400: the `[#27842]` docblock paragraph and the `disabledActions` describe, mirrored at `protocol.mdx:1335`) says the list is "never part of `etag`" and "a read that carries it is never answered `notModified`". Read against `protocol.ts:14473–14577` these stay literally true of the PROTOCOL method's `etag` and `notModified` fields, so they are not false; but the reason given ("a 304 would keep the caller on the list it was served before the switch") now describes a problem the REST layer solves, and a reader of this schema alone will conclude the HTTP read is never 304. Add one clause pointing at the REST door's fold so the two schemas read as one mechanism. Not a FAIL on its own.
- Tried to break the fold: (a) weak ETags — `W/"…"` is built after the fold and `normalizeIfNoneMatch` strips both forms, fine; (b) `undetermined` mask posture returns no ETag before the fold, fine; (c) cross-dimension collision between `audienceFingerprint` and `disabledActionsFingerprint` when one is empty — a theoretical 32-bit FNV collision of a withheld-view-name set against a JSON list string, the same property the existing intake/audience dimensions already have; not a finding; (d) the fold reads `result.disabledActions` as the protocol returned it, the same reference the envelope serves — no second read, no skew.
